findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] Comma-joined shard list used as a metric tag value (tags={"shard": "0,2,4"}) on spans.buffer.flusher.produce, segment_size_bytes, and wait_produce; commas are DogStatsD tag separators so the tag splits into invalid tags (shard:0, 2, 4) and the shard dimension is corrupted/lost, hitting the default config (--flusher-processes 1) where one process handles all shards

[Medium/concurrency] In thread mode (produce_to_pipe set), an unhealthy ("hang") thread is never stopped: the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard skips kill() and there is no other stop mechanism, yet _create_process_for_shards starts a replacement; the old hung thread can resume later, leaving two flusher threads concurrently flushing the same shards causing duplicate segment flushes/produces, and repeated hangs accumulate threads up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS

[Medium/test] The added time.sleep(0.1) ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to lambda _: None at the top of the test, so the intended synchronization never happens and the race this change was meant to fix remains (flaky test)

[Medium/performance] The memory-based backpressure check in submit now calls get_memory_info() on every per-process buffer (N sets of live Redis INFO round-trips per submitted message vs 1x before), and each restart creates yet another SpansBuffer with its own Redis client in the parent, scaling with flusher_processes

[Medium/test_gap] No test verifies that spans are actually flushed/produced correctly when shards are distributed across multiple flusher processes (test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural counts like len(processes) and map sizes), and the multi-process restart/health-check path is untested

[Medium/api] SpansBuffer(shards) assumes a shard-aware constructor and shard-scoped poll_flushed_segments/record_stored_segments/get_memory_info, but no change to SpansBuffer appears in this diff (the factory otherwise constructs SpansBuffer() with no args); if __init__ doesn't accept shard ids, flusher creation raises TypeError at startup and the buffer-side contract this feature depends on is unverified

[Low/api] max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) means the factory default flusher_processes=None silently yields one process per shard, contradicting the documented/click default of 1 ("Defaults to 1"); any non-CLI construction path that doesn't pass the new option changes behavior from 1 flusher process to N (more processes, more Redis clients)

[Low/bug] Inconsistent tag key for the same value: spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={"shards": ...} while produce/segment_size_bytes use tags={"shard": ...}, breaking metric consistency for dashboards/alerts

[Low/doc_defect] Comment "Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" describes per-shard health checking that the code does not perform; health is tracked and enforced only at the process level
[Low/bug] _create_process_for_shard is dead code; it is never called anywhere in the diff (restarts go through _create_process_for_shards directly)

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] Comma-joined shard list used as a metric tag value (tags={"shard": "0,2,4"}) on spans.buffer.flusher.produce, segment_size_bytes, and wait_produce; commas are DogStatsD tag separators so the tag splits into invalid tags (shard:0, 2, 4) and the shard dimension is corrupted/lost, hitting the default config (--flusher-processes 1) where one process handles all shards

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the code builds `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and uses it as a single metric tag value, e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`. When `--flusher-processes` is left at the default 1, one process can handle multiple shards, producing values like "0,2,4". For DogStatsD-style tag encoding (comma-separated tag list), commas inside a tag value will be parsed as separators, corrupting the intended `shard` dimension and potentially creating stray tags like `2`/`4`. This is a real, diff-introduced issue in metric tagging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] In thread mode (produce_to_pipe set), an unhealthy ("hang") thread is never stopped: the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard skips kill() and there is no other stop mechanism, yet _create_process_for_shards starts a replacement; the old hung thread can resume later, leaving two flusher threads concurrently flushing the same shards causing duplicate segment flushes/produces, and repeated hangs accumulate threads up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe` set), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` and starts it as a daemon, but `_ensure_processes_alive` only attempts to stop unhealthy workers via `process.kill()` guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. For threads, no stop/terminate is performed, yet `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` is called to start a replacement. Since both old and new threads run `SpanFlusher.main` for the same `shards` (and each has its own `SpansBuffer(shards)`), a previously “hung” thread that later resumes can concurrently flush/produce for the same shards, causing duplicate work and unbounded thread accumulation until the restart limit triggers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] The memory-based backpressure check in submit now calls get_memory_info() on every per-process buffer (N sets of live Redis INFO round-trips per submitted message vs 1x before), and each restart creates yet another SpansBuffer with its own Redis client in the parent, scaling with flusher_processes

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the memory-pressure code path changed from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` call to iterating all per-process buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`), so the number of `get_memory_info()` invocations per submitted message now scales with `len(self.buffers)` (i.e., flusher processes) instead of 1. Also, `_create_process_for_shards` creates a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` each time a process is (re)created and stores it in `self.buffers[process_index]`, meaning restarts recreate buffer/clients rather than reusing an existing buffer object. This is a diff-grounded performance/resource concern rather than a correctness bug (the exact Redis round-trip cost isn’t shown here, but the multiplied calls are).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No test verifies that spans are actually flushed/produced correctly when shards are distributed across multiple flusher processes (test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural counts like len(processes) and map sizes), and the multi-process restart/health-check path is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `SpanFlusher` to shard-to-worker mapping, multiple worker creation (`_create_processes`, `process_to_shards_map`), per-worker health/backpressure tracking, and restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive`. The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts structural properties (e.g. `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, shard distribution counts) and does not assert that flushed segments are actually produced correctly when shards are handled by different workers. Additionally, none of the tests exercise the unhealthy/restart paths introduced in `_ensure_processes_alive` (hang detection, kill/recreate per worker, restart limit). This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] SpansBuffer(shards) assumes a shard-aware constructor and shard-scoped poll_flushed_segments/record_stored_segments/get_memory_info, but no change to SpansBuffer appears in this diff (the factory otherwise constructs SpansBuffer() with no args); if __init__ doesn't accept shard ids, flusher creation raises TypeError at startup and the buffer-side contract this feature depends on is unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new call site `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` in `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, and then relies on `buffer.assigned_shards` to size/process-map shards. No corresponding `SpansBuffer` API changes are shown in this PR, so this change implicitly depends on `SpansBuffer.__init__` accepting a list of shard ids and on the buffer’s methods behaving correctly when instantiated per-shard subset. Whether this is an actual runtime bug (e.g., `TypeError`) cannot be verified from the diff alone, but the newly introduced constructor usage is a concrete contract assumption that should be verified/covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) means the factory default flusher_processes=None silently yields one process per shard, contradicting the documented/click default of 1 ("Defaults to 1"); any non-CLI construction path that doesn't pass the new option changes behavior from 1 flusher process to N (more processes, more Redis clients)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` makes `max_processes=None` (the factory default: `flusher_processes: int | None = None` and passed through as `max_processes=self.flusher_processes`) resolve to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, yielding `num_processes = len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (one process per shard). This contradicts the new CLI option help/default (`click.Option(... default=1, help="... Defaults to 1.")`) and also changes the non-CLI default behavior from the prior single-process implementation (`_create_process()` previously created exactly one process/thread).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] Comment "Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" describes per-shard health checking that the code does not perform; health is tracked and enforced only at the process level

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include the comment `# Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy` in `_ensure_processes_alive`, but the code only evaluates `process.is_alive()` and `time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[process_index].value` (process-level liveness/health), with no per-shard health evaluation beyond tagging metrics per shard. This makes the comment slightly misleading, but it’s a low-impact documentation nit rather than a verifiable behavioral defect or an important non-bug issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] _create_process_for_shard is dead code; it is never called anywhere in the diff (restarts go through _create_process_for_shards directly)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` (`src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`), `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly added but there is no call site in the diff. Process restarts in `_ensure_processes_alive` go directly to `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, and initial startup uses `_create_processes()` → `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. Thus the method is dead/unreachable as shown, which is a maintainability issue rather than a functional defect.
